guides.title: Getting started
guides.html:
Every call goes to the API's base URL, with your API token:

https://your-domain/api/v1

Your token is on the API page of your account. Check that it works:

curl -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
     https://your-domain/api/v1/me

The answer is the user the token belongs to.

Send the fields of a request as a form (application/x-www-form-urlencoded) or as JSON (Content-Type: application/json). The bulk import takes JSON. In a form, send a yes/no field as 1 or 0. Answers are JSON, except the log downloads, which are files.

Lists, contacts and campaigns are named by their uid, a 13-character identifier such as 6adaabbf98847. A contact is named by its id, a number: the same address has a different id in each list it belongs to.

guides.title: Authentication
guides.html:
Send your API token with every request, in a header:

curl -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
     https://your-domain/api/v1/lists

or as the api_token query parameter:

curl -H "Accept: application/json" \
     "https://your-domain/api/v1/lists?api_token=YOUR_API_TOKEN"

Always send Accept: application/json. Without it, a missing or wrong token is answered with a redirect to the sign-in page instead of a 401.

A customer's token reaches that customer's lists, contacts, campaigns and automations. An admin's token reaches the admin calls: customers, subscriptions, sending servers and maintenance. What each admin token may do follows the permissions of its admin.

Keep the token secret: it acts as its user, and the login-token call turns it into a signed-in session. To change a token, generate a new one on the API page.

guides.title: Errors
guides.html:
The HTTP status says what went wrong. The body says why, in one of these shapes:

  • a message: {"message": "Campaign not found"}, sometimes with "status": 0 or "status": "error";
  • the fields that failed, each with its messages: {"from_email": ["The from email must be a valid email address."]};
  • for the newer calls, both: {"message": "…", "errors": {"type": ["…"]}}.

Each call lists the statuses it answers with. The most common:

Status Meaning
400 The request misses something the call needs.
401 The token is missing or wrong, or its user may not act on this object.
403 The call refuses the request: a field is wrong, or the account may not do this.
404 Nothing has this uid or id.
409 The object is not in a state that allows the call (already subscribed, archived, …).
422 The request is well formed but refused; the message says why.
429 Too many calls; wait a minute.
